use_case: Orchestrate Python-based data pipelines, ETL/ELT jobs, analytics workflows, and scheduled automation.
Turn ordinary Python functions into observable, retryable, production workflows with minimal framework overhead.
Run flows locally, in containers, Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, or Prefect Cloud/self-hosted server.
pros: Very Pythonic: workflows are normal Python functions with decorators, type hints, async support, and normal testing/debugging tools.
Good developer experience for data teams: scheduling, retries, caching, state tracking, logs, UI monitoring, and dependency visualization.
Portable execution model: can start locally and deploy to multiple infrastructure targets without rewriting workflow logic.
Supports dynamic runtime behavior, event-driven triggers, automations, and human approval pauses.
cons: Best aligned with Python data/application workflows; less natural for polyglot distributed systems than Temporal.
Durability model is workflow-orchestrator oriented, not the same as Temporal-style deterministic replay of application state.
Operational features may require running Prefect server/Cloud and managing deployments, workers, and infrastructure blocks.
For complex cross-service transactions, compensation, and very long-lived business processes, Temporal is usually stronger.
